Trading 212

Bring your portfolio and holdings into Dayframe with a read-only key pair.

Use a key with Account data and Portfolio read permissions. The secret is encrypted by Dayframe and is never saved in this browser.
Not connected
StatusNot connected
Last syncedNever
AccountLive · read only
iWhere do I get these?
  1. Open Trading 212 and switch to the Invest or Stocks ISA account you want to connect.
  2. Open Menu → Settings → API (Beta), accept the warning, then choose Generate API key.
  3. Name it Dayframe and enable read-only Account data and Portfolio permissions. Leave order permissions off.
  4. Generate the pair, then copy both the API Key and API Secret Key. The secret is shown only once.
  5. Choose the matching Live or Demo option above and paste both values.
Using an IP-restricted key may block Dayframe’s Cloudflare connection. If that happens, create an unrestricted key but keep it read-only.

Portfolio Pies
Understand, build and optimise your T212 pies
🥧 What is a pie?
T212's way of auto-investing across multiple stocks at once
A pie is a portfolio within your portfolio. You set a target allocation — e.g. 40% AXTI, 30% AAOI, 30% LITE — and T212 automatically splits every deposit or dividend across your stocks in those exact proportions. It removes emotion from investing: instead of manually deciding how much to put into each stock each time, the pie does it for you.
✅ Good for
Themes you want to hold long term · Drip-feeding money in regularly · Keeping diversification on autopilot
❌ Not ideal for
Short-term trades · Stocks you want to exit quickly · Anything where timing matters
💡 Pro tip
Build pies around themes — CPO supply chain, space economy, AI infrastructure — not random collections of stocks
🤖 How should I distribute my stocks?
Groq suggests a pie structure based on your current holdings
Press "Get suggestion" — Groq will analyse your holdings and suggest how to group them into pies and what allocation each stock should have

Paper Trading
Practice trades with fake money — learn before risking real cash
What is paper trading?
You log a trade as if you bought or sold — but with no real money. The app tracks what would have happened. After a few weeks you can see: would you have made money? Would you have panic-sold at the wrong time? It is the safest way to learn how traders like @AskLivermore operate before putting real cash on the line.

AI Data Centres
🏗️
Every AI model in the world runs inside a physical building full of computers. Those buildings need power, chips, memory, cooling and cables to function.
When you use ChatGPT, Google search or Netflix recommendations, a data centre somewhere is doing the work
These buildings are being built at unprecedented speed — trillions of dollars of investment over the next decade
The companies supplying the components inside them get paid regardless of which AI company wins
You do not need to pick the winning AI product — you just need to own parts of the supply chain
$5.2T
projected spending by 2030
40M
homes worth of new electricity needed
7
layers — all must exist for AI to work
Tap any layer to learn more
Layer 0 — Glass & Substrates
LPK
▼
Computer chips sit on a base material, similar to how a building sits on foundations
Traditional base materials expand and contract with heat at a different rate than chips — causing micro-cracks over time at very high speeds
Glass expands and contracts at nearly the same rate as chips, making it a much more stable foundation
This transition is just beginning and will take 2-3 years to become mainstream — it is a long-term setup, not a near-term trade
LPK
Layer 1 — Power
CEG · VST · GEV · PWR — nuclear is the only 24/7 solution
FOUNDATION
▼
A single large AI data centre uses as much electricity as a city of 50,000 people
Solar panels stop generating at night. Wind turbines stop when there is no wind. AI data centres need power every hour of every day without interruption
Nuclear power stations run continuously regardless of weather — this is why Microsoft, Google and Amazon are all signing long-term nuclear deals
Microsoft signed a 20-year contract with Constellation Energy (CEG) to buy the entire output of a restarted nuclear plant — 20 years of guaranteed income from one deal
CEGVSTGEVPWR
Layer 2 — AI Chips
NVDA · ARM · INTC — the processors that run every AI model
PICKS & SHOVELS
▼
NVIDIA makes the specialist processors (called GPUs) that AI models run on — they have over 80% of the market and a waiting list over a year long
ARM does not make chips — instead they design the instruction set that nearly every chip in the world is built around, and collect a small royalty each time one ships
Intel makes the general-purpose processors (CPUs) that handle everything in a data centre that is not pure AI — and as AI becomes more automated, data centres need far more of these too
NVDAARMINTCAMDAVGOTSMTSEM
Layer 3 — Memory
MU · SNDK · DRAM ETF — 2026 supply sold out
STRUCTURAL SHIFT
▼
Memory is where a chip stores information while it is actively working — the more memory, the more complex the task it can handle
AI models are so large that they require a special high-speed type of memory called HBM, which is stacked directly on top of the chip to allow data to flow 10 times faster than normal
Only three companies in the world make HBM: Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung — Micron's entire 2026 supply is already sold to NVIDIA
For the first time ever, AI data centres now buy over half of all memory chips sold globally
MUSNDKDRAM ETFASMLAMATLRCX
Layer 4 — Cooling
VRT — every major data centre uses the same supplier
QUIET WINNER
▼
A rack of AI chips generates enormous amounts of heat — data centres spend 30-40% of all their electricity just on keeping things cool
Vertiv makes the cooling systems, power distribution and thermal management equipment inside virtually every major data centre
Google, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta all buy from Vertiv — there is no credible competitor at their scale
As data centres get bigger and chips run hotter, Vertiv's products become more valuable, not less
VRT
Layer 5 — Optical Networking
AAOI ✓ · AXTI ✓ · AEHR ✓
KEY BOTTLENECK
▼
Inside a data centre, thousands of chips need to communicate constantly — they are connected by cables
Traditional copper cables generate too much heat and cannot carry data fast enough at the speeds AI now requires
The solution is sending data as pulses of light through fibre optic cables — this is a massive industry-wide upgrade happening right now
The companies making the components for this transition are booked out years in advance — see the full breakdown on the dedicated CPO page
→ Full CPO breakdown
AAOI ✓AXTI ✓AEHR ✓
Layer 5b — GPU Cloud
NBIS ✓ · APLD ✓ · IREN · VIVO
HIGH GROWTH
▼
Most companies that want to use AI cannot afford to build their own data centre — it costs billions of pounds and takes years
Instead they rent computing power by the hour, the same way you rent a car rather than buying one
Applied Digital (APLD) builds the physical data centre buildings. Nebius (NBIS) fills them with computers and rents time to AI companies
VIVO is a small Norwegian data centre powered by cheap hydroelectric power — no tenant signed yet, but this is exactly the setup Applied Digital had before landing its first large contract
NBIS ✓APLD ✓IRENVIVOTRT
Layer 6 — AI Applications
Google · Microsoft · Meta · Amazon
DEMAND
▼
These are the companies spending hundreds of billions building AI products — their spending funds every layer below
The key insight: you do not need to pick which AI product or company wins
If you own the power companies, chip makers, memory suppliers and networking equipment — you get paid regardless of who comes out on top
Optical Networking & CPO
💡
The cables inside AI data centres have hit a physical limit. The entire industry is switching from copper to light.
AI data centres need thousands of computers to communicate constantly — the cables connecting them matter enormously
Copper cables overheat and slow down at the speeds AI now requires — this is a hard physical limit, not a preference
Fibre optic cables carry data as pulses of light instead — they run cooler, carry more data and use 75% less electricity
The companies making the components for this transition are selling out years in advance
75%
less power than copper
1.6T
latest generation speed — AAOI expanding to 930K/month
Sold out
Lumentum booked until 2028
Tap any layer to learn more
Layer 0 — Epitaxy Equipment
VECO · AIXA · ALRIB
▼
To make a laser chip, special crystal layers need to be grown one atom at a time in a high-precision vacuum chamber — this process is called epitaxy
The machines that do this are extremely specialised, cost millions each, and take months to install and qualify
These companies receive their orders and get paid before a single laser chip ever ships to a customer
Veeco specifically makes the type of machine (MBE) that AAOI uses for its highest-performance laser chips
VECOAIXA.DEALRIB
Layer 1 — Raw Materials
AXTI ✓ · SOI
▼
Ordinary silicon cannot generate light, so it cannot be used to make laser chips — a special crystal called Indium Phosphide (InP) is required instead
AXTI is one of only a handful of companies in the world that supplies this material at scale
When AAOI expands its factory, the demand for AXTI's crystals increases proportionally — the two are directly linked
Soitec (SOI) has a near-monopoly on a different specialist wafer used in the next generation of photonic chips — and each next-gen module needs four times more of it
AXTI ✓SOI
Layer 3 — Lasers
LITE · SIVE ✓ · COHR
BOTTLENECK
▼
Laser chips are the tiny components that convert electronic data into pulses of light — every fibre optic connection needs one at each end
Lumentum (LITE) is the leading maker of these chips and is completely sold out until 2028 — no new customers can even join the waiting list
NVIDIA invested £2 billion directly into Lumentum to secure its own supply — that is how critical this component is
Sivers (SIVE) makes a different type of laser chip used in both data centre networking and autonomous vehicle sensors
LITESIVE ✓COHR
Layer 4 — Transceivers
AAOI ✓ · VIAV
CURRENT REVENUE
▼
A transceiver is the module that plugs into a server and connects it to a fibre optic cable — each server needs one for every cable it connects to
AAOI manufactures these and has more orders than it can currently fulfil — revenue is growing over 130% per year
They announced plans to produce 930,000 modules per month by the end of 2027 — all for what appears to be a single customer
Viavi (VIAV) makes the testing equipment that every single module must pass before it ships — no module can be sold without it
AAOI ✓VIAV — watchSMOP.OL
Layer 5 — CPO Modules
POET · MRVL
▼
CPO (Co-Packaged Optics) is the next generation — instead of a removable module, the laser is built directly into the computer chip itself
This removes several components and reduces power consumption further, but it is still early-stage and not yet mainstream
If a small component fails in a CPO system, it can damage a very expensive chip — this is the main reason adoption is slower than expected
POET has confirmed that Marvell (who makes custom chips for Amazon and Google) is their first major customer
POETF — IBKRMRVL
Layer 6 — Testing
AEHR ✓ · VIAV · TRT
▼
Before any chip or module can be shipped to a customer, it must be tested under extreme conditions to find any hidden defects
AEHR runs chips at high temperature for hours before they are even cut apart from the wafer — catching faults at the earliest and cheapest point
Viavi validates the completed module right before it ships — every module AAOI makes must pass this test
As production scales to hundreds of thousands of modules per month, the revenue from testing scales proportionally
AEHR ✓VIAV — watchTRT
🔭 What's next: Plasmonics — the generation after photonics. You already hold AEHR and SIVE which play both.
Memory & Storage
🧠
Every AI model needs somewhere to store information while it is running. AI needs far more storage than anything that came before it.
Memory is where a chip keeps data it is actively working on — the more memory, the more complex the task
AI models are enormous — they require a new type of ultra-fast memory that sits directly on the chip itself
This is creating a permanent step-change in how much memory every device needs — not just data centres but phones, cars and laptops too
Three companies in the world make the most critical type — and all their supply is already sold out
4–16x
more memory AI servers need vs standard servers
50%
of all memory chips now bought by data centres
300GB
memory a self-driving car will eventually need — today: 16GB
Tap any layer to learn more
HBM — High Bandwidth Memory
MU · DRAM ETF
BOTTLENECK
▼
HBM is stacked directly on top of the AI chip in layers, like floors of a building, so data does not have to travel far — this makes it 10 times faster than normal memory
Only Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung make it — no other company has the technology
Micron's entire 2026 production is already sold to NVIDIA before it is even made
Useful signal: when Samsung announces price increases for memory, Micron's stock tends to follow around 4-6 weeks later
MUDRAM ETFASML
NAND Flash Storage
SNDK · KXIAY
▼
NAND flash is the type of storage used in SSDs — it saves data permanently, unlike memory which resets when power is removed
As AI models process larger amounts of information at once, every server needs more SSD storage to hold that data
SanDisk (SNDK) is smaller than Micron, which means its stock can move more sharply in both directions on the same news
Kioxia (KXIAY) is a Japanese NAND maker — pure-play exposure to the same demand without HBM exposure
SNDKKXIAYLRCXAMAT
Space & Earth Data
🚀
Space has moved from a government experiment to a commercial industry worth hundreds of billions.
Private companies can now launch satellites at a fraction of what it cost governments 20 years ago
This is creating new industries: global satellite internet, daily satellite photography of the entire Earth, military surveillance and communications
Governments are major customers — defence agencies need secure communications, navigation and intelligence from space
The barriers to entry are enormous — building rockets and spacecraft takes billions of pounds and years of expertise
$2B+
RKLB order backlog
52+
successful launches
$805M

Launch (RKLB ✓)
The only listed commercial launch company at scale besides SpaceX
YOU HOLD
▼
To put anything in space, you need a rocket — Rocket Lab is the only publicly listed company doing this reliably at commercial scale outside SpaceX
They have launched over 52 times successfully and have more than £2 billion of contracts in their backlog, including £805 million from the US Department of Defence

Individual Stocks vs ETFs
Two ways to invest. One tries to beat the market. One just owns it. Neither is wrong — but they suit different people and different goals.
📈 Individual Stocks
Higher risk · Higher potential return
✓
Can outperform the market significantly
✓
You choose exactly what you believe in
✓
No ongoing management fee
✗
One bad pick can wipe out your gains
✗
Requires research and time
✗
Emotionally harder to hold through dips
📦 ETFs (e.g. S&P 500)
Lower risk · Matches the market
✓
Instant diversification across hundreds of companies
✓
Historically beats most active investors long-term
✓
No research required — set and forget
✗
You will never beat the market
✗
Small ongoing fee (usually 0.07–0.2% per year)
✗
You hold companies you would not choose yourself
Tap any section to learn more
What exactly is an ETF?
Clear explanation — no jargon
▼
An ETF (Exchange Traded Fund) is a single investment that holds hundreds of companies inside it
When you buy one share of a S&P 500 ETF, you instantly own a tiny piece of all 500 companies in the index — Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Amazon and 496 others
If the market goes up, your ETF goes up. If it goes down, your ETF goes down. You get exactly the market average — no better, no worse
Think of it like buying a food hamper instead of individual items — you get a bit of everything in one purchase
What returns can you realistically expect?
Historical data — and the uncomfortable truth
▼
S&P 500 ETF — historical
~10%
average per year over 50 years. Some years -30%, some +30%.
Individual stocks — reality
90%
of individual stock pickers underperform the S&P 500 over 10+ years
The uncomfortable truth: most professional fund managers — people who do this full time with research teams and Bloomberg terminals — also fail to beat the S&P 500 consistently over a decade
That said, some individual stocks genuinely can outperform massively — AAOI, AXTI and AEHR in your portfolio have done exactly this. The challenge is finding them before they move, not after
The right mindset: the S&P 500 is the baseline everyone is trying to beat. If you are not beating it, you would have been better off buying the index
How the risk is completely different
This is the most important thing to understand
▼
An ETF holding 500 companies can only go to zero if all 500 companies fail simultaneously — this has never happened. The worst modern crash (2008) dropped the S&P 500 by 57%, but it recovered fully within 4 years
An individual stock can go to zero. It happens regularly — even at large, well-known companies. One piece of bad news, a fraud discovery or a product failure can permanently destroy the investment
The practical rule many investors follow: ETF as the foundation, individual stocks as the upside bet. If all your stock picks go wrong, the ETF keeps compounding. Your stocks are the bonus, not the safety net
✅ Your setup: Your T212 ISA holds a mix of individual stocks across specific themes. Adding a core ETF position (S&P 500 or Global All World) as a foundation would reduce the overall risk of the portfolio while keeping all your thematic upside.
Why people choose individual stocks over ETFs
The honest reasons
▼
You have specific insight: If you understand the photonics supply chain, spotted AXTI before it ran 5,000%, or know a sector better than the average investor — that is real edge that an ETF cannot give you
Theme exposure: The S&P 500 gives you about 4% exposure to semiconductor companies. If you believe photonics is the biggest infrastructure story of the decade, an ETF will barely move when AAOI runs 200%
Staying engaged: An underrated point — someone who researches their stocks and understands why they own them is less likely to panic-sell in a crash. Panic selling at the bottom is how most retail investors lose money
S&P 500 valuation: At certain times the index is expensive by historical measures, meaning future expected returns from the index are lower. Individual stocks in specific sectors may offer better risk/reward
Popular ETFs for UK investors
The most common options — what they hold and why
▼
S&P 500 — VUAG / VOO / SPY
Most popular
500 largest US companies. ~10%/yr historical average. Top holdings: Apple, NVIDIA, Microsoft. Fee: ~0.07%. The standard baseline everything is compared against.
Global All World — VWRP / ACWI
3,000+ companies across 50 countries. Less concentrated in the US. Lower potential upside than a pure S&P 500 but more diversified.
Nasdaq 100 — QQQ / EQQQ
100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies — heavily tech weighted. Higher returns in tech bull markets, falls harder in downturns. Twice as volatile as S&P 500.
Semiconductor — SOXX / SMH
Concentrated semiconductor exposure — NVIDIA, TSMC, ASML, AMD, Broadcom. Gives you the sector without having to pick individual winners.
DRAM ETF — Roundhill
In your portfolio
Memory chip focused — SK Hynix 26%, Samsung 23%, Micron 17%. The only practical way to hold SK Hynix and Samsung from a UK ISA.
How most serious investors think about this
🏗️
Foundation
S&P 500 or Global ETF — always compounding, guaranteed market return, nothing to monitor
🎯
Conviction positions
Individual stocks you have researched — AAOI, RKLB, NBIS. Sized 5-15% each for high conviction.
🎲
Speculative
Small bets where you accept you could lose everything — VIVO, POET, NAK. Keep under 2-3% each.
